lines.text: When two pulses meet on a rope, what shape does the rope take at their overlap? The answer follows from adding what each pulse would do at the same point.

The principle of superposition states, when two or more waves of the same type meet at a point, the resultant displacement is the algebraic sum of the displacements of the individual waves at that point. Displacement is signed and instantaneous. For example, plus three millimetres and minus two millimetres combine to plus one millimetres. Amplitude is the maximum possible displacement of one wave and must not replace displacement in the statement. The principle applies whenever waves of the same type overlap, equal amplitude, coherence and opposite travel directions are not prerequisites for superposition itself.
Stationary waves are a special outcome of superposition, the opposing progressive waves repeatedly combine to produce a fixed pattern.
Add instantaneous, signed displacements at the same point. Resultant displacement equals their algebraic sum. Equal amplitudes are not required for superposition.
Two pulses have displacements plus four millimetres and minus three millimetres at one point. Explain which quantities you add and why the resultant is positive.
How could you observe a wave pattern that stays in place even though its component waves move? Use reflection to send a wave back through the incident wave.

For microwaves, aim a transmitter at a metal reflector and move a detector along the path. Alternating signal maxima and minima reveal the stationary pattern. For a stretched string, drive it at a suitable frequency while a reflected wave returns from the end, stable loops appear with nodes between them. For an air column, use a sound source and vary frequency or column length until resonance. The closed end is a displacement node and the open end a displacement antinode, assuming negligible end corrections. Powder in a horizontal tube gathers where air displacement amplitude is small, at nodes. These observations all arise from superposition of incident and reflected waves.
The fixed minima and maxima in each apparatus are the nodes and antinodes used to analyse formation and wavelength.
Microwave, transmitter, reflector, moving detector. String, driver, reflected wave, stable loops. Air column, resonance, closed end node, open end antinode. Powder gathers at displacement nodes.
Describe one measurement or observation that shows a stationary wave in each of the three apparatuses.
A snapshot of a string can cross equilibrium in many places. Which of those places stay still through an entire oscillation?

Two progressive waves of the same type and frequency, with similar amplitudes, travel in opposite directions and superpose. To construct the stationary wave graphically, draw both profiles on a common position axis and add their signed displacements point by point. Repeat at later instants. A node is a fixed point where the resultant amplitude is zero, so displacement is always zero. An antinode is a fixed point where the amplitude is maximum. At a particular instant even an antinode can have zero displacement, so one snapshot is insufficient to establish a node. All particles between adjacent nodes oscillate in phase, particles in neighbouring loops oscillate in antiphase.
The sequence of fixed nodes and antinodes supplies a spatial ruler for determining wavelength.
Opposite directions, same frequency, similar amplitudes. Add two profiles point by point at successive times. Node, zero amplitude, antinode, maximum amplitude. Adjacent loops oscillate in antiphase.
How would two displacement snapshots distinguish a genuine node from a point momentarily at equilibrium?
The wave moves back and forth, but the node positions stay fixed. Their spacing lets you measure the travelling waves wavelength.

Adjacent nodes are separated by lambda over two, as are adjacent antinodes. A node and its nearest antinode are separated by lambda over four. Thus, if adjacent nodes or adjacent antinodes are a distance d apart, lambda equals two d. To reduce measurement uncertainty, measure the distance between positions several intervals apart, divide by the number of intervals, then double. For example, the first to fifth node spans four intervals. In an air column the closed end is a displacement node and the open end an antinode, the shortest resonant closed open column has L equals lambda over four when end corrections are negligible. A fixed fixed string's shortest pattern has L equals lambda over two.
Once wavelength is known, the progressive wave relation v equals f lambda can give frequency or speed when the other quantity is supplied.
Adjacent nodes or antinodes, lambda over two. Nearest node to antinode, lambda over four. Count gaps, average their separation, then double. Closed open fundamental, L equals lambda over four.
The first and fourth nodes are zero point nine zero m apart. Explain the interval count before finding the wavelength.

Two progressive waves meet at a point. Which condition must be met for superposition of the waves to occur?
Waves of the same type can superpose. Coherence is unnecessary for superposition itself.
The principle of superposition states that a certain quantity is added when two or more waves meet at a point. What is this quantity?
Instantaneous displacement is summed. Amplitude is a maximum, not the quantity added at each point.
Two waves of the same type overlap. When does the principle of superposition apply?
Any overlapping waves of the same type superpose. Equal amplitude is only relevant to perfectly deep stationary wave nodes.
What happens when two waves superpose at a point?
Displacements add algebraically at the point. Adding amplitudes would ignore the signs and instantaneous phases.
Which statement concerning a stationary wave is correct?
Particles within adjacent nodes are in phase. B is wrong because antinode amplitude is the sum of contributing amplitudes.
Two progressive sound waves move in opposite directions and superpose to form a stationary wave. Which statement describes an antinode of this stationary wave?
An antinode has maximum stationary wave amplitude. D instead describes a node.
Two progressive waves overlap. What is an essential condition for the two waves to form a stationary wave?
Opposite propagation directions are essential to form a stationary pattern. D gives travelling overlap instead.

The fundamental closed open pipe has L equals lambda over four, so f equals three hundred and twenty over open bracket four times ten close bracket equals eight hertz. D treats the entire pipe as one wavelength.

A stationary wave is set up in a stretched string. Which distance is equal to the wavelength of the wave?
Adjacent antinodes are lambda over two apart, so doubling that distance gives wavelength. C leaves it undoubled.

eight point one Stationary waves.
In one breath.

When waves of the same type overlap, their instantaneous displacements add. Two waves travelling in opposite directions can produce a fixed pattern of nodes and antinodes, whose spacing reveals wavelength.
Key ideas.

The principle of superposition says that when two or more waves of the same type meet at a point, the resultant displacement equals the algebraic sum of their individual displacements at that point. Add signed displacements, not amplitudes, a crest displacement of plus three millimetres and a trough displacement of minus two millimetres give plus one millimetres at that instant. The waves continue through one another.

A stationary wave forms when two progressive waves of the same type, frequency and similar amplitude travel in opposite directions and superpose. Reflection commonly supplies the returning wave. The resulting pattern does not travel along the medium. A node is a fixed position of zero amplitude, its displacement is zero at all times. An antinode is a fixed position of maximum amplitude. At some instants every particle can pass through equilibrium, a zero displacement at one instant therefore does not prove a node.

A graphical construction makes the formation clear. Draw the incident and reflected wave profiles on the same position axis at one time. At each position add their signed vertical displacements to draw the resultant curve. Repeat a quarter of a period later. Positions where the sums remain zero are nodes, positions with the largest motion are antinodes. Particles within one interval between adjacent nodes oscillate in phase. Across a node, the next loop oscillates in antiphase.

The solid and dashed curves show opposite extreme displacements of the same stationary wave, half a period apart, they are not the two component waves. N marks fixed nodes at zero, lambda over two and lambda, A marks antinodes halfway between. The bracket spans lambda over four from a node to its nearest antinode. Node and antinode positions stay fixed while the string oscillates.

Method.

To demonstrate a microwave stationary wave, aim a transmitter at a metal reflector. Move a detector between them and record regularly spaced signal minima or maxima. The incident and reflected microwaves superpose.

For a stretched string, drive one end at a suitable frequency while the returning wave reflects at the other end. Look for stable loops, with fixed nodes between them. For an air column, drive it with sound and vary frequency or column length until resonance. A closed end is a displacement node, an open end is a displacement antinode when end corrections are negligible. Fine powder in a horizontal tube gathers at displacement nodes, where air motion is least.

Mark several successive nodes or antinodes. The separation d of adjacent positions of the same kind is lambda over two, so lambda equals two d. Between a node and its nearest antinode the distance is lambda over four. Measuring across several gaps reduces the effect of uncertain positions, divide the total distance by the number of gaps before doubling.
Worked example.

The first and fifth nodes on a string are zero point eight zero m apart. There are four adjacent node gaps, so each gap is zero point eight zero over four equals zero point two zero m. lambda equals two open bracket zero point two zero close bracket equals zero point four zero metres. The fifth node is four intervals from the first, not five.
Traps.

Trap, Add the two amplitudes whenever waves meet. Why it's wrong, Amplitude is a maximum, the waves may have displacements of opposite signs at that instant. Instead, Add signed, instantaneous displacements at the stated point.
Trap, Call every zero crossing a node. Why it's wrong, An antinode also crosses equilibrium during each cycle. Instead, Identify a point that remains at zero displacement throughout the cycle.
Trap, Treat adjacent nodes as one wavelength apart. Why it's wrong, They are half a wavelength apart. Instead, Count the gaps and use lambda equals two d.
Exam technique.

For explain, say that the two progressive waves overlap, travel in opposite directions and have the same frequency, connect their superposition to fixed nodes and antinodes. For describe an experiment, name the source and reflector, what is moved or adjusted, and what observation identifies the pattern. For determine wavelength, show the number of node or antinode intervals and keep the unit with the final answer.
